segments: And many of them were stripped of horses,
and on foot they returned without having achieved anything.
Now the head over them had been the great noyan Abatai,
and he also, when he turned back and reached Assyria,
became afflicted with a severe sickness.
And after the return of these,
the Turkmens grew bold,
and made a large gathering,
and about a thousand horsemen from the army of the Egyptians joined them.
And they came from the direction of Marash,
to enter into the low-lying {OCR?} country of Cilicia once again.
And when King Leon perceived it,
he assembled his own Armenian force,
and set at its head his uncle Baron Smbat the Constable,
and others of the grandees.
And they went and met the Turks near Marash on Friday of the third week of the holy forty-day fast.
And on that very day that Baron Smbat, the uncle of the king, was killed,
and others of the grandees:
the lord of Kirbiza (or Karbezag?),
and thirteen others of the notables,
and three hundred horsemen.
And also many fell from among the Turks,
and they turned back, not being able to enter the country.
And before these things took place,
that is to say, in the first week of this fast,
on Wednesday, the 19th
(or 17th) of the month of Shebat in the year 1587
violent winds blew in Mosul and Erbil and their territory,
and bore a great deal of red sand,
so that the air was obscured,
and no one could see his companion,
from three o'clock until nine o'clock.
And trembling fell upon the people,
and they thought that on that very night they would be swept away by an atmospheric deluge,
or by an earthly earthquake,
like the city of Argish,
and they went out and passed the night outside their houses, in the plain.
And when the wind subsided,
they returned to their homes.
For also on the Sunday of the Departed,
which was before the beginning of the fast,
the wind brought much sand,
though not like this other one.
And at this time, the commander of Ḥiṣn Zāyid,
the one named Bīshār (or Begār?),
a wicked man and a shedder of blood,
an old man a hundred years of age,
resolved to flee to the Egyptians.
Because he harbored resentment in his heart against Mar Sarkis, the bishop of the Armenians in the city of Erzincan,
who was a great and honored man before the Mongol kings,
he planned to kill him and then depart.
